result.title: Monotone Viability Learning for Offline Safe Reinforcement Learning
result.summary: Offline safe reinforcement learning requires reliable long-horizon safety estimates from fixed data. Learning Hamilton-Jacobi (HJ) viability in this setting calls for semantic preservation, convergence, and numerical stability. To address these challenges, we propose Monotone Viability Learning (MoViL), which learns viable sets from offline transitions through monotone finite-horizon set recursion. The recursion preserves finite-horizon safety semantics and converges to the infinite-horizon viability kernel. Binary supervision maintains a fixed target scale across horizons, avoiding discount-induced numerical attenuation. We further establish sufficient conditions for recovering behavior-supported viable subsets. The learned viability estimates are used to certify actions at deployment. Dubins car experiments validate the numerical accuracy of the learned viable sets. Evaluations on safe RL benchmarks demonstrate state-of-the-art reward-cost performance. MoViL satisfies the average cost constraint on every task and achieves the lowest average cost among the compared methods. These results highlight MoViL's potential to extend long-horizon HJ viability analysis to safety-critical systems where reliable dynamics models are unavailable and online exploration is unsafe.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 MoViL，通过单调有限时域集合递推从离线转移数据学习 Hamilton-Jacobi 可行集，用二值监督避免折扣导致的尺度衰减，并在部署时用学到的可行性估计认证动作。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「单调跨时域递推 + 跨时域固定尺度监督」可能为 latent 推理中的长度泛化与停止决策监督提供线索，可供核查；但研究对象是安全 RL 的状态可行性，与视觉多模态推理无直接关联。
